transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I just can’t shut my brain off anymore. It starts with something small, like a client not responding, and then within a few minutes I’m thinking I’m going to lose the contract, fall behind on divorce payments, and never get back into a real leadership role. It just keeps going, and I can’t seem to stop it.
Do you find that you often feel on edge, tense, or overly worried about things even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Yes. I feel wound up almost all day, even when there’s nothing urgent going on. My shoulders stay tight, like I’m bracing for bad news, and I’ll catch myself pacing around the house or bouncing my leg on calls for no real reason. It’s like my body is tense before anything has even happened.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, even when there’s no clear reason for it?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’m sad for no reason exactly, and I haven’t really thought about it that way. I guess I’ve been pretty worn down, but I don’t know if I’d call it losing interest.
Have you noticed feeling down or losing pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even for a day or two, even when things are going okay?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed it in that way. I mean, I get worn out and distracted, but I can’t say there are specific days where I’m just down or not enjoying things when everything else is okay.
Have you ever had periods lasting several days or more where you felt down or lost interest in things, even when you weren’t particularly stressed or worried about anything?
I don’t think so. I can’t point to a stretch of several days where I felt down or stopped enjoying things when I wasn’t also stressed or worried. It’s hard for me to separate it out, honestly.
When you’re not actively stressed or worried about something, do you ever find yourself feeling empty, unmotivated, or like things just aren’t as enjoyable as they used to be?

I don’t really think so. When I’m not stressed or worried, I don’t usually notice feeling empty or like things aren’t enjoyable. I may be tired, but I can’t say I’ve had that kind of feeling on its own.
Have you ever noticed feeling down, losing interest in things, or not getting pleasure from activities you usually enjoy, even when there wasn’t anything stressful or worrying going on at the time?

No, I don’t think I’ve noticed that. If there’s no stressful or worrying thing going on, I can’t really say I feel down or stop enjoying things. It’s more that those feelings, if they come up, seem tied to being worried about something.
Have you ever felt down, lost interest in things, or stopped enjoying activities you usually like, even when there wasn’t anything stressful or worrying happening at the time?
Not that I can really identify, no. If I’m feeling down or not enjoying things, it’s usually because I’m worried or stressed about something. I don’t remember it happening just out of nowhere.
Have you ever noticed that, even when you’re not stressed or worried about anything, you still feel down, lose interest in things, or stop getting pleasure from activities you usually enjoy?

No, I haven’t really noticed that happening on its own. If I feel down or less interested, it seems connected to being stressed or worried about something. I can’t think of a time where I felt that way when things were otherwise okay.

Have you ever noticed feeling down, losing interest in things, or not enjoying activities you usually like for at least a couple of days, even when you weren’t stressed or worried about anything during that time?

No, I don’t think so. I can’t really separate it out that way—if I’m feeling down or not enjoying something for a couple days, there’s usually some worry or stress tied to it. I don’t remember it happening when I wasn’t worried about anything.
Have you ever had a period where you felt down, lost interest in things, or couldn’t enjoy activities for two weeks or more, even when you weren’t particularly stressed or worried about anything?
No, I don’t think I’ve had that. If I’m down or not enjoying things, it’s usually tied to worry or stress. I can’t recall a two-week stretch where it happened without that being part of it.

Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt down, lost interest in things, or couldn’t enjoy activities you usually like for at least two weeks, even when you weren’t stressed or worried about anything during that time?

No, I don’t think I’ve had that kind of two-week period. When I’ve felt down or not into things, it’s been tied up with being worried or stressed. I can’t really think of a time where it happened without that.
Have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things almost every day for at least two weeks, even when you weren’t particularly stressed or worried about anything?
No, not really. I don’t think I’ve had that kind of stretch where I felt down or uninterested almost every day for two weeks unless there was stress or worry going on.
Have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day for two weeks or more, even when there wasn’t anything stressful or worrying going on at the time?

I don’t think so. I know we’ve talked about this, but I can’t remember a period like that where it was just feeling down or not interested for two weeks without something stressful or worrying behind it.
Have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day for two weeks or more, even when there wasn’t anything stressful or worrying going on at the time?

I’m still not coming up with an example of that. If I’ve felt down or not interested in things, it’s usually been connected to being worried or stressed about something, not out of nowhere for two weeks or more.
Have you ever had a period lasting two weeks or more where you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day, even when there was nothing stressful or worrying going on at the time?

No, I don’t think I’ve had that. When I’ve felt low or not interested in things, it’s been tied to stress or worry. I can’t think of a two-week period where it happened without something like that going on.
Have you ever had a time when you felt down or lost interest in things nearly every day for two weeks or more, even when there wasn’t anything stressful or worrying going on at the time?
I don’t think so, no. I know I’ve answered this a few times, but I really can’t point to a stretch like that unless there was some stress or worry going on.
